requirements.title: Serve MCP over streamable HTTP with session semantics
requirements.body: Vision MUST expose MCP endpoints using the go-sdk StreamableHTTPHandler per server port. The server MUST support initialize, GET event streaming, and session teardown via DELETE while honoring Mcp-Session-Id semantics.

scenarios.title: Initialize returns a server session id
given: Vision daemon is running with a configured MCP server port
A client sends a valid initialize request
scenarios.when: The initialize request is handled by the streamable endpoint
then: Response is successful and includes Mcp-Session-Id
The session id can be used by follow-up requests

scenarios.title: Session teardown invalidates further use
given: A client has an active streamable session
The client sends DELETE for that session
scenarios.when: A later request reuses the deleted session id
then: The request is rejected as an unknown or expired session
No previous session resources remain attached

scenarios.title: Disconnect-triggered cleanup reaps stale sessions
given: A shared-mode stdio server or managed-http gateway has an active upstream session
The client disconnects the session-bound GET/SSE receive stream without sending DELETE
scenarios.when: The configured disconnect grace period expires after the last session-bound GET/SSE stream closes
then: The upstream session is removed from tracking
Admission capacity is freed for new sessions
The shared downstream subprocess or managed HTTP backend remains healthy for other sessions
A canonical reap reason is recorded in lifecycle metrics

scenarios.title: Idle zero-ref reaping tears down shared downstream
given: A shared-mode server has zero upstream sessions (all removed)
idle_reap_timeout is configured (non-zero, non-negative)
scenarios.when: The idle reap timeout expires with no new sessions arriving
then: The shared downstream subprocess is terminated
A structured audit event is logged with server name, PID, and idle duration
The next GetOrCreateSession spawns a fresh downstream subprocess
Admission state is unaffected (already at zero)

scenarios.title: POST completion does not trigger disconnect cleanup
given: A shared-mode stdio server or managed-http gateway has an active upstream session
A normal POST request with Mcp-Session-Id completes successfully
scenarios.when: No DELETE is sent and no session-bound GET/SSE stream closes
then: Vision does not start the disconnect grace period for that POST completion
The upstream session remains tracked
No session.disconnect_detected event is emitted for ordinary POST completion

scenarios.title: Application activity re-arms managed-http disconnect grace
given: A managed-http lease has no open GET/SSE stream and is inside its disconnect grace window
An application request for the same session arrives before the window expires
then: The lease is not reaped by the original disconnect deadline
Application activity extends the disconnect grace window
The lease remains tracked while the re-armed window is open

requirements.title: Enforce subprocess isolation per MCP session (stateful) or shared subprocess (stateless)
requirements.body: Vision MUST maintain strict 1:1 mapping between each upstream MCP session and a supervised downstream subprocess when the server is configured with stateful: true. When the server is configured with stateful: false (default), multiple upstream sessions MAY share a single downstream subprocess managed by a SharedSessionManager. Session teardown or timeout MUST terminate only the owning subprocess (stateful) or decrement the shared refcount (stateless).

scenarios.title: Concurrent clients receive isolated subprocesses
given: Two clients connect concurrently to the same server port
Both establish independent MCP sessions
scenarios.when: Each client performs tool calls and receives notifications
then: Each session maps to a different subprocess
Notifications and responses are routed to the correct session only

scenarios.title: Session timeout cleans up deterministicly
given: A session exceeds idle timeout or absolute TTL
then: The owned subprocess is terminated gracefully then forcefully if needed
The session mapping is removed and cannot be reused

scenarios.title: Concurrent clients share a single subprocess for stateless servers
given: A server is configured with stateful: false (default)
Two clients connect concurrently to the same server port
Both establish independent MCP sessions
then: Both sessions route tool calls through the same shared downstream subprocess
The shared subprocess is alive as long as at least one upstream session is active
When the last upstream session disconnects, the shared subprocess is eligible for teardown

requirements.title: Apply security and admission controls to all streamable endpoints
requirements.body: Vision MUST require bearer authentication, enforce a strict Origin allowlist, reject wildcard CORS, and enforce configured limits for max concurrent sessions, request sizes, and HTTP timeouts on streamable MCP endpoints.

scenarios.title: Unauthorized and disallowed origin requests are denied
given: A request is missing valid credentials or has a non-allowlisted Origin
scenarios.when: The request hits a streamable MCP endpoint
then: The request is rejected
No session or subprocess is created

scenarios.title: Admission limits reject excess sessions
given: Configured max concurrent sessions is reached
then: The request is rejected with a clear limit error
Existing sessions remain healthy

requirements.title: Preserve operational compatibility and emit migration observability
requirements.body: Vision MUST preserve existing daemon command and health endpoint behavior while adding structured lifecycle/security logs for session creation, teardown, timeout, subprocess spawn/kill, and request denials.

scenarios.title: Daemon and health contracts remain stable
given: The Streamable migration is deployed
scenarios.when: Operators run daemon lifecycle commands and health checks
then: Daemon start/status/reload/stop remain functional
The admin /health response shape remains backward-compatible: the status enum stays ok|degraded|unhealthy and no field is removed
/healthz remains a pure daemon liveness probe and is unchanged
The condition that triggers degraded is governed by rq-mcpstr05, which derives it from client-observable reachability rather than process liveness alone
The per-server /health endpoint is out of scope for this compatibility scenario; its contract is defined by rq-mcpstr05

scenarios.title: Lifecycle and denial events are observable
given: Sessions are created, timed out, denied, and torn down during normal operation
then: Logs include session and server identifiers for lifecycle and denial events
Operators can correlate subprocess lifecycle with session lifecycle

requirements.title: Report client-observable server reachability accurately
requirements.body: Vision MUST derive reported server status from client-observable MCP reachability independently of process liveness. Reachability MUST distinguish unprobed, probing, reachable, and unreachable states; absence of successful probe evidence MUST NOT be reported as healthy. Probes MUST record depth-specific evidence and reason, and MUST classify a server as unreachable only after three consecutive failures at the applicable depth.

scenarios.title: Unreachable MCP endpoints report non-healthy across transports
given: A configured server uses stdio, managed-http, or an HTTP/SSE proxy transport
The server process may be alive, but its MCP endpoint cannot establish or serve a client session
scenarios.when: The server status is evaluated after reachability probing
then: The server is reported as non-healthy for each of the three transports
The reported reachability state is not reachable
The status includes a reason identifying the client-observable reachability failure

scenarios.title: Missing probe evidence is not inferred as healthy
given: A server has no successful reachability probe evidence
scenarios.when: A status surface reports the server state
then: The server is not reported as healthy
The reachability state remains unprobed or probing until successful evidence exists
Process liveness alone does not make the server reachable

scenarios.title: Ordered lifecycle delivery preserves restart reachability
given: A server restart produces Stop and Start lifecycle events in close succession
The events are submitted to the lifecycle delivery mechanism
then: Events are delivered in one FIFO order
The Start handler cannot be followed by a late Stop handler that tears down the newly created listener
A restart cannot leave the server reported as healthy or reachable when no listener is bound

scenarios.title: Failed managed gateway reload reports non-healthy
given: A managed-http server is being reloaded
Construction of its managed gateway fails
scenarios.when: The reload result is reflected in server status
then: The server is reported as non-healthy and not reachable
The status includes a reason identifying the managed gateway construction failure
A prior healthy or reachable status is not retained without current successful probe evidence

scenarios.title: Reachability probes leave no session or capacity residue
given: A reachability probe runs at listener, session, or idle-server end-to-end depth
The probe may create a temporary MCP session
scenarios.when: The probe succeeds or fails and completes cleanup
then: No temporary MCP session remains tracked after the probe
The probe does not consume admission capacity after completion
An end-to-end probe removes its temporary session using the normal session teardown path
